tldr: For the specified exact-quota binary-covariate Gram--Schmidt walk, the actual retained-pivot terminal law converges in total variation at the certified rate \(O_{\overline B}(n^{-1/5})\) to a computably evaluated, nondegenerate finite lattice law \(L_\phi\). On the maintained constant-effect critical subclass, the unadjusted HT error has limit \(\beta L_\phi+sN\), and a total original-record mixture interval preserves this benchmark, including atoms and vanishing residual variation. Feasible regression adjustment removes the prognostic lattice term: its interval uses only normal calibration, recovers the causal effect exactly on regular zero-scale records, and has limiting scaled radius \(s\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\), strictly smaller than the HT benchmark when \(s>0\). A bounded constant-effect witness in the broader published outcome space has a non-Gaussian HT limit even after standardization by its true design variance; positive coverage remains restricted to the stated critical subclass.
gap: The exact-count modification is specified in HSSZ Supplement S8.4.2 but is outside its main analysis. CDG residual normality does not evaluate the constrained terminal imbalance at bounded residual energy. Finite-support computation alone gives no effective limiting CDF.
